items.title: Trace DOM sources to dangerous rendering sinks
items.objective: Determine whether URL, message, storage, API, or DOM data reaches HTML or script execution sinks.
prerequisites: A clean supported browser profile and first-party application assets/traffic
A realistic attacker-controlled client source or owner-approved static-code review path
steps: Identify the client source, trust boundary, processing code, and final DOM/storage/network/worker sink
Use a unique inert synthetic marker through a realistic application-controlled path
Trace behavior in raw responses, loaded code, parsed DOM, storage, messages, and network activity
Reproduce the harmless effect in a clean profile and clear all test state

examples.note: Use a clean browser and inert local marker; client-side presence alone is not proof of exploitability.

items.manipulate: One URL/message/storage/object/property/resource/navigation/client-state value at a time through a realistic attacker-controlled path
items.secure_behavior: Client code treats all external and persisted values as untrusted data, uses safe DOM/URL/message/storage APIs, minimizes origin privilege, and relies on server controls for security decisions.
items.vulnerable_behavior: a realistic attacker-controlled source produces harmless same-origin execution
items.validation: Trace source to security-relevant sink/effect in a clean browser and establish realistic attacker delivery plus server/origin impact; code patterns alone are insufficient.
false_positives: dangerous APIs can receive only fixed trusted templates
manual console changes are not an attacker delivery path
items.impact: A confirmed client-side weakness can execute script, spoof trusted UI, leak browser-held data, load untrusted resources, persist across offline caches/workers, or expose protected server functionality through missing backend controls.
evidence: Source-to-sink trace and relevant first-party code excerpt
Clean-browser reproduction with inert marker
Origin, account, storage/worker/message, CSP, and delivery context
Network/server effect where applicable plus test-profile cleanup
